findings.pdf_says: Declarative procedures ... 1 DEB 1 DEB Z / DECLARATIVES ... 1 DEB 1 DEB Z / END DECLARATIVES ... 1 DEB 1 DEB Z (the obsolete-element flag Z is printed at the right margin after each 3RD STD '1 DEB' entry; the glyph is partly clipped at the page edge, exactly as the Z flags on page 734 are)
findings.why_it_matters: The Z flag marks the element as obsolete (to be deleted in the next revision) in the 3rd standard; the three DEB rows lose it, so the summary no longer records that the Debug-module uses of declaratives are obsolete. Page 734's transcription keeps the same clipped Z glyph as 'Z'.

findings.why_it_matters: The printed ELEMENT column is indented to show which element each row qualifies (e.g. 'Operands must be of equal size' is a sub-entry of 'Comparison of nonnumeric operands', 'USING phrase' of 'Procedure Division header'); the transcription flattens every row to one level, unlike the neighbouring pages (737, 739, 740) which keep the nesting with   indents, so the parent of each sub-entry is lost.

findings.why_it_matters: The printed ELEMENT column nests each phrase under its statement (and TERMINAL under INPUT, each ALSO under TRUE/FALSE or WHEN); the transcription flattens all rows to one level, so statements and their phrases are indistinguishable and the two 'ALSO phrase' rows lose the parent that distinguishes them. Neighbouring pages 740 and 742 keep the nesting with   indents.
